raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
PlotEqualTo and PlotNotEqualTo previously fell back to raw strings when float parsing failed, causing "true" and "false" filter strings to never match boolean DataFrame columns. This resolves boolean targets to bool when comparing against boolean-valued series (including nullable series with missing values), while preserving literal comparisons for string columns and existing float/inf behavior.

Fixes #60629

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Thanks for addressing #60629. Independently verified `ef5ccf673619a3a2df164696ab46950ae438ac34`: the 39 PR filter tests and 10 additional compatibility cases pass on both macOS arm64 and Linux arm64 (49 checks per platform).

The additional cases cover equality/inequality, case-insensitive boolean targets, object and nullable-boolean columns with missing values, and literal string labels named `"true"`. The real plotting module CLI also writes the expected PNG; observing the rendered line gives `[(10, 20), (20, 40)]` for `enable_prefix_caching==true` on the synthetic fixture from the report. The reported case is resolved in these checks.

One remaining check: Ruff reports E501 at the two added parser cases in `tests/benchmarks/test_plot_filters.py:204-205`, and `ruff format --check` flags that file. Please apply the formatter before merge.

A documentation follow-up would also help users discover the supported syntax: add an example such as `--filter-by enable_prefix_caching==true` to `docs/benchmarking/sweeps.md`, noting that boolean targets are case-insensitive and string-valued labels remain literal.

Validation used focused benchmark dependencies and source imports, with no inference-engine/model/GPU or upstream CI execution. Codex assisted with this verification.

+    def _resolve_target(self, series: "pd.Series") -> bool | float | str:
+        target_lower = self.target.lower()
+        if target_lower in ("true", "false"):
+            import pandas as pd
+
+            s_clean = series.dropna()
+            if pd.api.types.is_bool_dtype(series) or (
+                len(s_clean) > 0 and all(isinstance(x, bool) for x in s_clean)
+            ):
+                return target_lower == "true"
+
+        try:
+            return float(self.target)
+        except ValueError:
+            return self.target
